name: AH-64 Apache
summary: The US Army's heavy twin-engine attack helicopter, with tandem crew stations, a nose sensor turret, a chin-mounted 30 mm cannon and Hellfire-carrying stub wings.

wings: Four-blade main rotor, often with a round Longbow radar dome sitting on top of the mast
Short stub wings with four pylons for Hellfire missiles and rocket pods
engines: Two engines in separate pods on either side of the fuselage behind the cockpit
Exhausts with angled 'black hole' IR suppressors pointing outward and back
fuselage: Tandem stepped cockpits with flat-plate glazing, gunner in front and lower
Large sensor turret (TADS/PNVS) on the nose with a 30 mm chain gun under the chin
Fixed main gear with long trailing legs and a tailwheel
Bulky avionics bays along both sides of the forward fuselage
tail: Four-blade tail rotor in an uneven 'X' (scissor) arrangement
Large horizontal stabilator mounted low at the base of the fin

tellTales: Ball-shaped radar dome perched on top of the main rotor (on radar-equipped aircraft)
Bulky angular nose turret above a cannon hanging under the chin
Wheeled gear with tailwheel under a narrow stepped tandem cockpit

confusedWith.howToTell: The Apache sits on tall wheeled gear with a tailwheel and bulky side engine pods; the Viper rests on skids and has a slimmer, smoother fuselage with engines blended on top.
Both have wheels and a tailwheel, but the Apache has a narrow tandem cockpit, nose turret and weapon wings instead of the Black Hawk's wide troop cabin.

usCount.source: US Army ~824 AH-64D/E (Army FY2026 aviation data / FlightGlobal World Air Forces 2025)
